slides.text:
The **domain** of a function is every input it accepts. A formula refuses an input when it would have to divide by zero.$$f(x) = frac{1}{x - 4}$$
Which input does this one refuse?
slides.explain: At $x = 4$ the bottom is 0, so $f(4)$ is undefined. Every other number is fine.

slides.text:
So the domain is every number except 4. Interval notation says “every number except 1” like this: $(-∞, 1) ∪ (1, ∞)$.
Write the domain of
$$f(x) = frac{1}{x - 4}$$
slides.label: Domain:
slides.hint: Everything below 4, joined to everything above 4.
slides.explain: Round brackets, because 4 itself is left out.

slides.text:
The other thing a formula refuses: the square root of a negative number.$$g(x) = sqrt(x - 3)$$
Which inputs are allowed?
slides.hint: The inside, $x - 3$, must be 0 or more.
slides.explain: $x - 3 >= 0$ means $x >= 3$. Zero inside a square root is fine: $sqrt(0) = 0$.

slides.text: Write the domain of $sqrt(x - 3)$ in interval notation.
slides.label: Domain:
slides.hint: It starts at 3, and 3 is included, so use a square bracket: $[3, ∞)$.
slides.explain: A square bracket means the endpoint is included. Infinity always gets a round bracket.

slides.text:
A **piecewise** function has more than one rule. The condition on the right says which rule to use.$$f(x) = cases{x + 1, x < 2; x^2, x >= 2}$$
Find $f(2)$.
slides.label: $f(2)$ =
slides.explain: $2 >= 2$ is the true one, so use $x^2$: $f(2) = 4$. Only one rule ever applies.

slides.text: On a graph, a filled dot is the value and an open circle is a gap. Find $f(1)$.
slides.hint: Two things happen at $x = 1$. Only the filled dot counts.
slides.explain: The filled dot is at height 2, so $f(1) = 2$. The open circle at height 4 is where the graph was heading.
